clue.text: One goes on the bottle as salary reaches ceiling

parts.note: screw is old slang for wages or salary
a ceiling is the top or upper limit

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink as their pay hits its upper limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One goes on the bottle' suggests a drinker; it is a cap that is screwed on to a bottle. 'reaches' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of cap is fitted on the neck of a bottle by twisting it.

clue.text: Blimey! Thin turn-out in Greek port

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey

indicators.note: the letters of thin are turned out of their order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised at the sparse crowd in a Greek harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-out' looks like an attendance figure, but it signals an anagram of THIN, making INTH after COR.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is a city and harbour on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece.

clue.text: Too menial, sadly to be passionate

indicators.note: sadly says the letters of too menial are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: Something too lowly is, unfortunately, meant to be fiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionate is ruled by strong feelings.

clue.text: One in diplomacy is taken for granted

indicators.note: in puts the single letter for one inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, delicate handling of people
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in the diplomatic world is assumed without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated.

clue.text: Noel's stage fun?

parts.note: Noel is Noel Coward, the English playwright; his stage fun is the title of one of his comedies, a play about a vain actor

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of a comedy by Noel Coward, and the answer is the title of exactly such a play.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1939 comedy by Noel Coward, a work written for the stage and full of mirth.

clue.text: Disconcerted in ceremonial seat, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to take the sound of the word for a ceremonial seat

parts.note: a throne is the ceremonial chair of a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone feels unsettled sitting in a grand chair of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown by something means being confused or put off balance.

clue.text: Barman rarely beats better half

parts.note: taps are light beats or knocks

indicators.note: half takes the second three letters of the six in better

explanation.surface: A bartender seldom thrashes his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse, but 'half' takes the back half of BETTER, TER. 'rarely' belongs to the definition: the word is now seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster, someone who draws beer from the tap, is an old-fashioned word for a barman.

clue.text: Feeling sorry for game in end of hunting

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: end of takes the closing letters, the -ing ending, of hunting

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the game at the close of a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' here takes the word's ending, ING, rather than its last letter alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it or be sorry about it.

clue.text: French dialect name given to everybody in court

indicators.note: in puts the word for everybody inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A French variety of speech gives its name to everyone at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' wants to be a royal or legal court; it is the verb, woo. 'given to' attaches N at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Walloon is the variety of French spoken in southern Belgium.

clue.text: Archduke, we hear, in revolutionary riot

indicators.note: revolutionary says the letters of riot are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An Austrian archduke is heard to be caught up in a revolutionary uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archduke' looks like a nobleman, but it is Beethoven's 'Archduke' piano trio; 'we hear' means it is a piece listened to, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Archduke is a piano work for three players, heard in concert.

clue.text: Processed pear in fresh cheese

indicators.note: in puts the reworked pear letters inside the word for fresh

parts.note: chilly weather is fresh, cool

indicators.note: processed says the letters of pear are worked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A treated pear goes into a fresh cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' points to processed cheese, but it signals an anagram: AERP goes into CHILLY after its C. CAERPHILLY is a crumbly Welsh cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a mild, crumbly white Welsh cheese named after its town.

clue.text: Flying linnets met in muster

indicators.note: flying says the letters of linnets and met scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds on the wing gather at a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustering soldiers means signing them up, so recruitment is the noun sense here.

clue.text: Good string wax

parts.note: a row is a string or line of things

explanation.surface: Quality cord needs waxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax' looks like a polish for the string; it is the verb, as the moon waxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to increase in size, as the moon does.

clue.text: Mate commonly in a church setting?

explanation.surface: A friend is found, colloquially, in a church setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate. 'setting' only says the pieces are put together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a friend is a china, short for china plate.

clue.text: For example, London's main plot

parts.note: Jack London, the American writer, wrote stories, so one of them is an example of London's work
a main is a supply line, as in a water main

explanation.surface: London's principal scheme is given as an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London's' looks like the city but is the writer Jack London.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a book or film is the sequence of events it follows.

clue.text: Oslo cubes crumbled in stew at sea

indicators.note: crumbled says the letters of Oslo and cubes break up and reform

explanation.surface: Stock cubes from Norway break up in a sailor's stew.
explanation.walkthrough: LOBSCOUSE is a sailors' stew of meat, vegetables and ship's biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobscouse is a meat and vegetable stew eaten by sailors.

clue.text: Farm butter glob Italy produces

indicators.note: produces says the letters of glob and Italy are worked into the answer

explanation.surface: A dollop of Italian farm butter is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts: a male goat on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat butts with its head, so on a farm it is the animal that rams.

clue.text: One rook smoke-damaged? How annoying!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of smoke are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A single crow harmed by smoke is an irritating thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the bird; it is the chess piece, R. 'damaged' turns SMOKE into KSOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or tiresome makes one exclaim at the nuisance.

clue.text: Creator's final blessing

parts.note: the Creator is God, so Creator's gives God's
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A divine maker gives a last benediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of good fortune, a blessing from heaven.

clue.text: At right-angles to length of aircraft, making Lincoln by morning

definitions.text: At right-angles to length of aircraft

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A president is flown across in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to the line of a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: What may come out of meal-tin?

definitions.text: What may come out of meal-tin?

indicators.note: may come out of says the letters of meal-tin can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Something might be poured from a food container.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: food is what comes out of a meal tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is food or nourishment, the stuff kept in a food tin.

clue.text: Superficially read set-end novel by Kipling

indicators.note: end takes one tip of the word set, here its front letter

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel about an orphan in India

explanation.surface: Someone skims a Kipling novel set at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-end' gives S, the front tip of SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a text is to glance over it quickly without detailed reading.

clue.text: Widow's contribution said to have clout?

indicators.note: said tells the solver to take the sound of the words for the widow's gift

parts.note: in the Gospel story the poor widow gives her mite, a tiny coin, to the temple

explanation.surface: Is a poor widow's small offering reckoned to carry weight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'clout' could be a blow; here it is power or influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means power or influence, strength to get things done.

clue.text: Chow-chow?

parts.note: chow is slang for food, and a chow is a breed of dog, so this is food for that dog

explanation.walkthrough: Chow-chow looks like a relish or the dog breed; read as chow for a chow, it is a dog's treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog, and chow is slang for food, so this is a snack for a dog.

clue.text: Ant, for example, not caught in place within

indicators.note: not says the letter for caught is taken out

parts.note: an ant is an example of an insect
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An ant, unlike others, escapes capture in a confined place.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset something is to set or fix it into a surrounding piece.

clue.text: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, you say?

definitions.text: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, you say?

parts.words: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, you say?
parts.note: spectacles used at the opera that are held up by a handle; Handel the composer sounds like handle

explanation.walkthrough: Handel's operas suggest musical shows; 'you say' turns Handel into the sound of handle, giving glasses on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorgnettes are eyeglasses mounted on a handle, used at the opera.

clue.text: Previously-owned house-dog inside

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the letters of house-dog

explanation.surface: A secondhand house dog is kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secondhand has belonged to someone else before.

clue.text: Group of five shut up these days

parts.note: pent means shut up or confined, as in pent-up
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Five people are kept quiet nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a set of five things.

clue.text: Departures from sanctuaries

explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawals from a place are departures, and quiet refuges are sanctuaries.
